claims.text: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) finished on top in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt with about 44% of the vote.
Germany's domestic intelligence agency has classified the AfD's branch in Saxony-Anhalt as a proven right-wing extremist group.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insists there can be no cooperation between mainstream parties and the AfD.
Friedrich Merz said the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt was the worst electoral defeat the CDU had suffered in decades and had shaken the party to its very foundations.
An exit poll in Saxony-Anhalt indicated that only 9% of voters approved of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's performance.
AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund is a 35-year-old former fragrance salesman.
The AfD won 44.5% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, while the Christian Democrats fell to 18.5%.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration has surpassed 1,413 consecutive days in office.
Preliminary election results show the AfD won 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, leaving it three seats short of an outright majority.
The CDU's share of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt almost halved to 17.2%.
US President Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the projected Saxony-Anhalt election results on Truth Social.
Convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic was buried in Belgrade in a service attended by thousands.
Ratko Mladic died in The Hague at age 84 while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity.
An EU spokesman stated that any glorification of war criminals, genocide denial, and revisionism contradict fundamental European values.
The United Nations war crimes court convicted Ratko Mladic of genocide over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, where around 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were killed.
Serbian Patriarch Porfirije personally officiated at Ratko Mladic's funeral service at the St Luka church in Belgrade.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic did not attend Ratko Mladic's funeral, citing a scheduled meeting with the president of Uzbekistan.
EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos canceled a planned visit to Belgrade following the military honors provided for Ratko Mladic's funeral.
A canopy collapse at the railway station in Novi Sad in November 2024 killed 16 people, triggering student-led protests in Serbia.
Free bus services were organized from Bosnia and towns across Serbia for people attending Ratko Mladic's funeral.
Fans of the Serbian football club Red Star Belgrade displayed an image of Ratko Mladic before their derby match against Partizan Belgrade.
Brent oil futures rose to around $97 a barrel, up 9% over five days and 19% over the past month.
US West Texas Intermediate crude rose to $92.27 a barrel.
US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, while Iran's IRGC stated it struck three tankers and three US-linked vessels.
Saudi Aramco's Jizan facilities were struck for the second time in a month.
The average US national petrol price reached $4.15 per gallon, while US diesel prices reached over $5.90 per gallon.
India's average crude oil import basket crossed $100 per barrel for the first time in six weeks, reaching $101.07 on Friday.
Iran and Oman are in the final stages of negotiating an agreement to establish a temporary safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.
Macquarie analysts estimated that around 7 million barrels per day of crude and refined fuels cross the Strait of Hormuz, down from roughly 20 million barrels per day before the conflict.
US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held separate weekend peace talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow and Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv.
Steve Witkoff stated on social media that substantive progress was made, including movement on scheduling additional trilateral talks.
UN Human Rights Chief Volker Turk called for an urgent ban on fully autonomous weapons following reports of autonomous drones killing people in Ukraine.
Ukrainian MP Lisa Yasko stated that Ukraine does not trust the talks and described US envoys' flattery towards Vladimir Putin as disgraceful.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Kyiv by train from Poland.
Russian President Vladimir Putin declared a three-day ceasefire to ensure the safety of the visiting US envoys.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy held three rounds of talks with US envoys, with national security advisers from the UK, France, and Germany joining the final round.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine will need a winter package of military assistance, including Patriot missile systems, if the war drags into winter.
Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed 13 people, including women and children, according to the Lebanese health ministry.
An Israeli overnight strike on a building in Kfar Rumman killed 11 people, including two children and four women.
A second strike in Kfar Rumman killed an 18-year-old rescuer affiliated with the Amal movement and wounded another.
Two Israeli soldiers were lightly injured during a close-quarters encounter near the Beaufort fortress after a Hezbollah member opened fire.
Lebanese health authorities reported that Israeli attacks across southern Lebanon killed at least 27 people over a three-day period.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called the strikes a dangerous escalation that jeopardizes the June US-brokered ceasefire.
The Israeli military stated it struck Hezbollah infrastructure after two explosive drones were launched towards its troops near the Ali al-Taher ridge.
An Amazon cargo Boeing 767-300 operated by 21 Air crashed after overshooting the runway at Miami International Airport, killing five people and injuring five others.
The cargo plane overran the runway and struck a Ford van carrying seven contract cleaning workers and a Toyota Corolla carrying three passengers.
The NTSB recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder from the crashed aircraft.
Amazon Air flight 7598 had flown from Cincinnati to Miami, Miami to San Juan, and was returning from San Juan to Miami at the time of the crash.
The cargo plane traveled approximately 1,300 feet past the end of the paved runway into a perimeter area near where Tesla robotaxis were stationed.
Miami International Airport is not equipped with engineered materials arresting systems (EMAS) at the end of its runways.
